record.context_brief: Conjectured dimension threshold for bubble towers
record.original_question: Is it true that for the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, bubble-tower sign-changing solutions in which at least two bubbles blow up at the same point on different scales can occur only in dimensions N >= 7 in the regime lambda -> 0?

evidence.quote: Moreover, it has been proved by Iacopetti and Pacella in [32] that the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) has no bubble-tower solutions, with two bubbles blowing up at the same point, in low dimensions 4 <= N <= 6 as lambda -> 0.
Conjecture 1: In a general bounded domain Omega, bubble-tower solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) can only exist for N >= 7 as lambda -> 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth domain with $N \geq 4$, and consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2} u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega,$$
where $2^* = \frac{2N}{N-2}$ is the critical Sobolev exponent and $\lambda > 0$. A "bubble-tower sign-changing solution blowing up at a point $x_0 \in \Omega$" is a family $\{u_\lambda\}$ of sign-changing solutions which, as $\lambda \to 0^+$, decomposes as
$$u_\lambda(x) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} (-1)^{j+1}\, \alpha_N\, \mu_{j,\lambda}^{(N-2)/2}\bigl(\mu_{j,\lambda}^2 |x-x_0|^2 + 1\bigr)^{-(N-2)/2} + o(1)$$
in $H_0^1(\Omega)$, with $k \geq 2$ concentration parameters satisfying $\mu_{1,\lambda},\dots,\mu_{k,\lambda} \to \infty$ and $\mu_{j+1,\lambda}/\mu_{j,\lambda} \to \infty$ (so at least two bubbles concentrate at the same point $x_0$ on different scales), where $\alpha_N$ is the standard normalization constant for the Aubin–Talenti bubbles.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded smooth domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, bubble-tower sign-changing solutions of the above form (with at least two bubbles concentrating at a common point) can exist as $\lambda \to 0^+$ only if $N \geq 7$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is partially established. Iacopetti and Pacella proved nonexistence of bubble-tower sign-changing solutions (with two bubbles at the same point) in low dimensions N=4,5,6 as λ→0. Existence constructions of such tower-of-two-bubbles sign-changing solutions are known for N≥7 (e.g., in symmetric/general domains). However, ruling out bubble-towers with more than two bubbles at the same point in arbitrary bounded domains in low dimensions, and the full statement of the conjecture in general domains, does not appear to have been completely settled in the literature available through 2025.

status_evidence.title: A nonexistence result for sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in low dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Iacopetti–Pacella prove nonexistence of tower-of-bubbles sign-changing solutions in dimensions N=4,5,6 as λ→0.
status_evidence.claim: Supports the low-dimensional nonexistence side of the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Sign-changing tower of bubbles for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of sign-changing tower-of-bubbles solutions for N≥7 in symmetric domains.

status_evidence.title: Nodal cluster solutions for the Brezis–Nirenberg problem in dimensions N≥7
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of nodal/bubble cluster solutions in N≥7.
status_evidence.claim: Existence side of the dimensional threshold.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis-Nirenberg problems: Open questions and new results in dimension six
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open questions for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in dimension 6.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing investigation of low-dimensional cases.
